text:
Alex P.: NovaMed turned on log export for the POC and were seeing missing trace links + intermittent 429s. Jordan, can you paste an example log line and your uploader config? :mag:

Jordan (NovaMed): Sidecar shows some 429s and traces not showing in the Console. Example: 
```
2026-08-21T13:12:01Z level=error code=429 req=nm-555 trace=bb7a2f event_count=450
2026-08-21T13:12:02Z info delivered=true req=nm-556 trace=bb7a30
```
Were batching ~450 events and use 8 parallel worker pods. Uploader is a lightweight Go sidecar that POSTs to /v1/drain.

Export Bot: Alert: export-backpressure (project "novamed-poc") - 429 spikes ~1100 rps over 3m. Ticket POC-5120 opened.

Maya T.: Two quick asks: 1) do you set a trace header (x-request-id or traceparent) on the request? 2) are you compressing payloads?

Jordan (NovaMed): We set X-Request-ID from app request id. No compression. Here's our curl-ish snippet from the sidecar: 
```
http.Post("https://export.redwood.com/v1/drain", "application/json", bytes.NewReader(batch))
setHeader("Authorization", "Bearer $TOKEN")
setHeader("X-Request-ID", reqID)
```

Ravi (SRE): Large batch size + 8 concurrent writers explains the 429s. Recommend: batch_size=250, workers=3. Also ensure we forward the exact header name the gateway expects. Our gateway config for on-prem drains defaults to `trace_header: x-request-id` but can be customized.

Eli (Solutions): For trace linking the Console expects `traceparent` (W3C) or `dd-trace-id`. If NovaMed can't emit W3C, we can map `x-request-id` -> `traceparent` at the gateway. Quick gateway mapping: 
```
map_headers: { "x-request-id": "traceparent" }
```
We can push that mapping for the POC.

Sophie (Sec): Note NovaMed POC contains PHI. Before export we must remove patient identifiers. Provide sample jq filter to remove fields and hash emails: 
```
jq '.events |= map(del(.patient_ssn, .patient_name) | .user.email |= ("sha256:" + (.|@text)))' batch.json > scrub.json
```
I'll add the formal sec answers to the ticket.

Ravi (SRE): I applied a temporary rate cap on export gateway: `export_rate_limit=900` for novamed-poc and enabled header passthrough for `x-request-id`. Monitoring: https://console.redwood/internal/exports/novamed-poc (internal).

Jordan (NovaMed): After lowering batch size and workers, 429s dropped to near 0 in the last 5m. Trace click-through still missing for some entries (trace id bb7a2f shows nothing).

Eli (Solutions): If some app requests generate non-standard trace IDs we might need to normalize. Send a sample of the app-generated request id and we'll create a small mapping rule (regex -> traceparent). Also check that the sidecar sets the header per event instead of only for the batch (we prefer per-event header or include per-event trace_id in payload).

Jordan (NovaMed): Sample req_id: nm-7f3cbb7a2f. We can change sidecar to include per-event trace_id in each event JSON.

Maya T.: Good plan. Adding per-event trace_id is best practice. Also toggle `enable_prefix_kv_cache=true` on your route to avoid duplicate forwarding if retries happen.

Sophie (Sec): Uploading scrub scripts and the PHI handling checklist to POC-5120. Remember: for Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS for exported blobs.

Export Bot: POC-5120 status -> mitigated (owner Ravi).

Alex P.: Sales note: include a POC export egress allowance (2GB/day) and mention egress pricing if they go Dedicated. Jordan, any other blockers? :thumbsup:

Jordan (NovaMed): All good for now. Will reopen if trace mapping fails for new traces. Thanks team. :pray:
